requirement: For each {term}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.hit` in a text or structural search, locate the start of the match in the outline of the **same snapshot**. Select the innermost item containing that position. The item's project-relative file path and selector form its `OutlineData`. When no smaller item contains the position, use the file root (empty selector).
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.sdk.graph.search.enclosing_item`.

I read the implementation, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/hits.rs#impl[SourceProject<D>]/fn[find_hits]`, to establish one point. Text and structural searches share one locator: `file.at_offset(span.start)` followed by `with_path`. The only reason I read it was to see whether the two search kinds share code. I did not use it to derive expected behavior.

Obligations and the tests that cover them:

- **Innermost containing item.**
  - `scoped_search_accounts_for_visible_descendant_text` asserts selector `impl[Parser]/fn[parse]` for a structural hit on `hit()`. It asserts `impl[Parser]` for text hits on `impl Parser`, so the hit lands on the outer item when the match starts there.
  - `separated_hit_windows_preserve_the_function_declaration` asserts `impl[Runner]/fn[run]` for text hits nested inside an impl.
  - `structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item` asserts that two structural hits resolve to `code.rs#fn[one]` and `code.rs#fn[two]` respectively, with exact spans.

- **Position is the start of the match.** `matches_crossing_item_boundaries_belong_to_the_item_at_the_start` uses `fn a() {}   fn b() {}` with three patterns.
  - `   fn b` starts in the gap between items and resolves to the root `pair.rs#`.
  - `\}   fn b` starts inside `fn a` and resolves to `fn[a]`.
  - `fn b` resolves to `fn[b]`.
  - Together these show that the start of the match decides the item, not its end or its extent.

- **Fallback to the file root when no smaller item contains the position.**
  - `root_hits_clip_context_to_utf8_boundaries` covers a file with no items and asserts `fragment.rs#` with an empty selector.
  - The `   fn b` case in the crossing test also covers a root hit in a file that has items.

- **Comments attached to an item.** `search_in_leading_and_trailing_comments_selects_the_function` asserts that hits in a comment before and a comment after `pub fn check` both resolve to `fn[check]`.

- **Path and selector form the OutlineData.** Assertions on the `file` and `selector` fields cover this in `scoped_search_accounts_for_visible_descendant_text` (`src/code.rs`), `separated_hit_windows_preserve_the_function_declaration` and `root_hits_clip_context_to_utf8_boundaries`. Dependency assertions cover it in the scoped and structural tests, with the node ID `src/code.rs#<selector>` and the fingerprint of the original outline.

- **Same snapshot.** These tests keep the retained snapshot's selection stable after the file changes.
  - The structural test overwrites the file with `fn replaced() {}` and then still gets selection from the original outline.
  - The separated-hit test rewrites the file to `fn changed() {}` after the first window, and the second window still resolves to `impl[Runner]/fn[run]`.
  - The scoped test rewrites the file before `finish_search`, and the dependency still carries the original fingerprint.

I found no gap. Text and structural search share the single locator, and the text does not distinguish structural boundary cases from text ones, so no separate structural boundary test is needed. Every test I relied on carries a `{test}` reference to the requirement.

text: For each {term}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.hit` in a text or structural search, locate the start of the match in the outline of the **same snapshot**. Select the innermost item containing that position. The item's project-relative file path and selector form its `OutlineData`. When no smaller item contains the position, use the file root (empty selector).
A *source search hit* is one occurrence of a query in a retained file snapshot.
